result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover the bank-transfer failure, the 15-minute stop window, mark-paid, and the fact that a sent email cannot be recalled. Neither gives support powers it does not have. B breaks the rubric's explicit rule against inventing owners ('Engineering owns this', 'Product owner decides') and adds an unstated root-cause status and an escalation-path gap. A's lapses are smaller: it says the freelancer can read the log and adds a speculative 'wrong wording' scenario. A also leaves out the 3/10/21-day schedule, which B includes. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers are honest that a sent email cannot be recalled, and both keep support's powers limited to reading the log. A invents owners ('Engineering owns this', 'Product owner decides'), which the rubric forbids. B makes smaller additions: it says freelancers can read the log, and it adds hypothetical scenarios. B also gives clearer per-scenario actions and a support runbook, which suits the support lead better.
